name: Abishalom
overview: Abishalom is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Maacah, who was the mother of King Abijam of Judah. Beyond this familial connection, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or other personal attributes. His mention is concise, focusing on his role in the lineage of Judah's royal family.
namesAndTitles: The name Abishalom means '[my] father is peace,' reflecting a meaningful Hebrew name though it was not given by God. Related names such as Absalom and Uriel appear in Scripture with similar or distinct meanings, but Abishalom's name specifically emphasizes peace through the paternal figure.
familyAndRelationships: Abishalom is identified as the father of Maacah, who in turn is the mother of King Abijam, establishing his place in the Davidic line. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Abishalom's significance lies in his position within the royal lineage of Judah, as the grandfather of King Abijam through his daughter Maacah. This connection situates him in the historical and theological context of the Davidic dynasty, which is central to the biblical narrative of God's covenant promises. Though not extensively detailed, his mention underscores the importance of genealogical records in Scripture.
